response = "The discrimination between rearrangement and contamination is settled empirically, by fixing first what the unexpected material actually is and only then asking where each of its carbon atoms came from. Before any structural analysis could be attempted, the unexpected product was isolated from the crude mixture by flash column chromatography, and only once pure material was in hand was that material submitted for mass analysis. High-resolution mass spectrometry provided the exact mass of the unexpected product. High-resolution mass spectrometry distinguishes constitutional isomers by their differing exact masses. The exact mass so obtained shows that the unexpected product and the intended product had identical molecular formulas. The two possibilities at this stage exclude one another: either the formulas of the unexpected and the intended product coincide, as the mass data report, or the unexpected product and the intended product had different molecular formulas, and exactly one of those two situations can hold. An authentic sample of the proposed rearrangement product was prepared by independent synthesis, and the comparison this made possible resulted in identical NMR spectra for the isolated unexpected product and that standard. Quantitative NMR indicated that the starting material contained less than 0.1 percent of other organic species. The starting material lot contained an isomeric organic impurity. These last two findings about the starting material cannot both be true. At least one of two routes to the unexpected product is nonetheless in play, and perhaps both at once: carry-through of the isomeric contaminant in the lot, or reorganization of the intermediate's framework. Before the reaction was repeated, carbon-13 was incorporated at a single defined position of the starting material, and this labelled substrate was then carried through precisely the conditions that had given the unexpected product. The carbon-13 label appeared at a different skeletal position in the unexpected product. Isotopic labels are randomly redistributed around the carbon framework during a Wagner-Meerwein rearrangement. The displacement of the label away from the site at which it was installed is itself evidence that the intended intermediate's skeleton reorganized under the reaction conditions, and it is this kind of positional bookkeeping on individual atoms, rather than any purity assay or formula determination taken on its own, that converts a plausible mechanistic story into a demonstrated one."
